5.1.rationale: The cited provisions refer to creating public awareness on issues of domestic violence and creating awareness of the characterizing features of domestic violence among state entities, but they do not explicitly address violence against women or gender-based violence specifically. Under the coding rules, domestic-violence awareness alone (without an explicit link to violence against women) is insufficient to count as information/education about VAW.

5.2.indicator: Information and education about gender equality
5.2.rationale: The retrieved sentences focus on domestic-violence awareness and implementation structures; they do not require or provide education/awareness activities specifically about gender equality or women's rights, nor do they explicitly link any such gender-equality education to preventing violence against women. A reference to gender balancing in appointments is not an educational/awareness activity.

5.3.indicator: Information and education about VAW laws and policies
5.3.rationale: While the text includes duties to advise victims of their rights and remedies under the Act, this is framed as victim assistance/response rather than a primary prevention activity disseminating information to the public or communities about VAW/DV laws and policies. The provisions do not specify public legal-awareness or dissemination campaigns about the law/policies as prevention measures.

5.4.indicator: Prevention through education and improving the quality of education
5.4.rationale: None of the candidate sentences identify schools, curricula, educational institutions, or education-quality improvements as measures to prevent violence against women (or even domestic violence). References to “educational competency” of board members or general awareness-raising are not education-sector/curriculum-based prevention measures.

5.5.rationale: The retrieved provisions do not establish prevention activities that specifically engage men or boys (e.g., programmes targeting men/boys, masculinity or gender-norm change initiatives) to prevent violence against women. References to perpetrator counselling/rehabilitation are post-incident responses and are not framed as primary prevention engaging men and boys generally.
